correctness.rationale: An inclusion-maximal matching leaves independent uncovered shores. Four points have 12 incidences, with at most six repeated incidences because a point pair shares at most one chosen line; at most three lines avoid those four points, ruling out size <=5. For three points, at least six lines are met, and equality (required for size six) needs one distinct available line for each pair. They form a noncollinear triangle with precisely the three allowed directions. Its horizontal/vertical corner and nonzero horizontal displacement give a unique displayed T_{x,y,a}; the three avoided lines are forced. For the reference triangle, three point-to-line edges are forced, and the remaining six vertices form a 6-cycle with two perfect matchings. Translation and simultaneous negation cover the other triangles. An independent increasing-edge-index enumeration visits each matching once and tests maximality by inspecting every edge for an uncovered pair, yielding {6:36,7:567,8:648,9:42}. It reproduces the published 36 masks and 126 exchange edges exactly. Among the 630 unordered pairs the needed exchanges are 3,4,5,6 with counts 126,54,270,180; thus one- and two-edge moves are impossible. Independent graph traversal gives degree seven, 108 triangles, and the common shell profile (1,7,12,12,4), establishing connectedness and radius and diameter four. The 108 direction-preserving affine collineations give one orbit on the 36 states. An extra independent check groups the two completions for each uncovered triangle as adjacent true twins; their 18-vertex quotient is isomorphic to Pappus, so the computed exchange graph is also Pappus[K_2].
residual_risks: The independent enumeration uses the affine incidence model. The frozen LCF source includes a separate explicit model isomorphism and minimum-layer proof, but its program was not executed.
This verifies endpoint batch exchanges, not a model that demands maximal intermediate matchings or reconfigures nonminimal matchings.

evidence: Adriaensen et al. study balanced incidence-free pairs; the symmetric-design equality of Theorem 1.2 and the symmetric-incidence-structure version in Theorem 5.8 require k>=100. Here k=3, and pair incidence varies with direction.
Bonamy et al. use perfect matchings with alternating 4-cycle flips. Dejter studies short-cycle structure and reattachments in Levi graphs.

value.rationale: The Pappus incidence graph is canonical, and minimum maximal matchings model minimum edge domination on it. Describing all optima by complementary affine triangles explains their geometry rather than just outputting 36. The exact jump from every optimum isolated at budget two to a single connected transitive graph at budget three is a meaningful finite reconfiguration cutoff with a useful complete distance profile. It cannot be read off from the optimum cardinality or from the previously known perfect matchings.
residual_risks: The scientific value is the exact natural-graph classification and sharp threshold, not a theorem for all Levi graphs or all reconfiguration models.
